title: Netflix has started production on your documentary
dek: Three episodes, one ominous drone shot, and a case that everyone in the comments has already solved. Twelve questions to find out which documentary you are.

results.name: THE VANISHING
results.tagline: Everything left behind, including the keys
results.blurb: Your documentary is about absence. A car in the drive, a phone still charging, a life with no obvious exit. Everyone has a theory and none of them fit, and the camera keeps returning to the same empty doorway as if it might answer this time.
results.watchOut: Disappearing is not the same as being mysterious. Somebody is waiting for a text.

results.name: THE CONFESSION THAT DIDN'T FIT
results.tagline: They said it. That was supposed to be the end
results.blurb: Your case has a confession in episode one and four episodes of doubt afterwards. You tell the truth at the worst possible moment, in the wrong tone, with details that make everyone lean back. Nothing about it is clean, which is exactly why people keep watching.
results.watchOut: Truth without timing lands as damage. Read the room before you unburden yourself.

results.name: THE SMALL-TOWN FEUD
results.tagline: Two families, one driveway, forty years
results.blurb: Your documentary is not really about the crime. It is about a fence, a boundary dispute and a grudge that got handed down like a christening gown. Everyone is extremely polite on camera and absolutely none of them are over it.
results.watchOut: You are carrying a grudge that predates you. Put some of it down.

results.name: THE PAPER TRAIL
results.tagline: Follow the money. It goes somewhere embarrassing
results.blurb: Your story is spreadsheets, second mortgages and a very reasonable-sounding man in a good coat. Nothing looks violent, everything looks normal, and the damage is a hundred small signatures. The documentary is three episodes of people saying they had no idea.
strengths: Sees the pattern in the numbers
results.watchOut: You trust a good presentation far too easily. Read the second page.

results.name: THE RECEIPTS
results.tagline: It was all in the group chat
results.blurb: Your documentary is a scrolling wall of messages, and every single person in them looks worse by episode three. You are the one who keeps screenshots, remembers who said what, and can produce the exact message from 11:48pm. You are not nosy. You are thorough.
results.watchOut: Not everything needs to be forwarded. Some things need to be let go.

results.name: THE COLD CASE
results.blurb: Your file is a box in a basement with a name on the side and a detective who retired still thinking about it. You are patient, understated and impossible to fully close. Every few years something surfaces and everyone remembers how much they cared.
strengths: Refuses to let things die quietly
results.watchOut: Some things need closing, not another review. Let one file rest.

results.name: THE DISAPPEARANCE OF A VERY ONLINE PERSON
results.blurb: Your documentary has a ring light in the background of every interview and a comment section doing its own investigation. You are extremely visible, extremely curated and slightly unknowable in a way that makes people refresh the page. The story is partly about you and partly about the audience.
strengths: Knows exactly what people want to see
results.watchOut: The audience is not the same as a friend. Log off and call one.

results.name: THE PERFECT ALIBI
results.blurb: Your documentary spends four episodes proving you could not have done it, and one uncomfortable minute suggesting you could have arranged it. You are careful, prepared and always exactly where you said you would be. Nobody can catch you out, which is somehow worse.
results.watchOut: Being unimpeachable is lonely. Let someone see the messy version.

results.name: THE NEIGHBOUR WHO NOTICED
results.tagline: Saw a light on at 2am. Told nobody for a year
results.blurb: You are the small, careful witness at the centre of everything: the one who saw the car, heard the argument, remembers the date. You do not want to be in the documentary. You are in the documentary. And you are, as it turns out, completely correct.
results.watchOut: Watching is not the same as helping. Speak up sooner next time.

results.name: THE UNSOLVED FINALE
results.tagline: Episode six ends on a question mark
results.blurb: Your documentary refuses to resolve. There is a theory, a suspect, a very compelling timeline, and then a title card that says the case remains open. Everyone finishes it furious and immediately starts a podcast about it. You would not have it any other way.
results.watchOut: Not every open question is profound. Some are just avoidance.
